1 What is Pendle?

Pendle is a yield tokenization protocol that fundamentally changes how you interact with yield-bearing assets. Instead of just holding your staked ETH and earning yield, Pendle lets you split that yield apart and trade each piece independently.

The core innovation is the PT/YT split — every yield-bearing asset (like stETH, wstETH, or aUSDC) can be tokenized into two separate tokens: PT (Principal Token) representing the underlying principal, and YT (Yield Token) representing the right to future yield payments.

Why does this matter? Because yield and principal have different values and different risk profiles. A trader who believes yields will rise might buy YT to amplify their exposure. An institutional player who wants to lock in a fixed rate might buy PT at a discount to par. Both can trade exactly the exposure they want — without needing a counterparty who wants the opposite of the full asset.

Pendle uses SY (Standardized Yield) tokens as the base representation. SY tokens are ERC-5111 assets that wrap yield-bearing positions in a standardized format. This allows Pendle to create a unified, liquid market for previously fragmented yield streams.

Key use cases: Fixed-rate lending (buy PT for guaranteed principal return), yield speculation (trade YT on yield direction), hedge existing yield exposure (institutions protecting against yield volatility), and harness strategies (farm extra yield from YT).

📌 PT (Principal Token)

Represents the underlying principal. PT trades at a discount to par because you're paying upfront for something redeemable at maturity. Example: if ETH APY is 4% and maturity is 1 year, PT might trade at ~$0.96 (you get $1.00 back at maturity = ~4% yield locked in).

📈 YT (Yield Token)

Represents the right to all future yield accruing on the underlying. If yield exceeds expectations, YT holders capture that upside. If yield drops, YT loses value. YT price = expected yield discounted to present value.

📈 Bull Case — APY rises to 7%

YT price increases as more yield is expected. You profit from the yield surprise. Higher APY → higher YT value.

📉 Bear Case — APY drops to 2%

YT price falls as less yield is expected. You lose as yield expectations collapse. Lower APY → lower YT value.

Implied Yield (market expectation)
Actual Yield (realized)
Implied Yield = PT discount annualized (1 - PT_price) / PT_price × (365/days_to_maturity)
Example: PT = $0.96, 90 days (1-0.96)/0.96 × 365/90 = 16.9%

9 Glossary
PT — Principal Token

The principal portion of a yield-bearing asset. Represents the underlying asset redeemable at maturity. Trades at a discount to par based on time and implied yield.

YT — Yield Token

The yield portion of a yield-bearing asset. Represents the right to receive future yield payments. Value = expected yield discounted to present.

SY — Standardized Yield

ERC-5111 token standard for yield-bearing assets. Provides a unified interface for representing wrapped yield positions across different protocols.

Implied Yield

The annualized yield derived from PT pricing. If PT = 0.96 with 90 days to maturity, implied yield = (1-0.96)/0.96 × 365/90.

Maturity

The date when PT can be redeemed for the underlying asset at par ($1.00). YT expires worthless at maturity. All yield has been accrued and paid.

Tokenized Yield

The process of wrapping yield-bearing assets into PT+YT. Separates the yield stream into tradeable components with different risk/return profiles.

Harness

A strategy where YT received from SY lockup is deployed in yield farming strategies. Amplifies total yield without uninvesting principal.

Spot Yield

The current yield rate being generated by the underlying asset (e.g., stETH APY). Different from implied yield which is forward-looking.

10 Risk Considerations
⚠️ Smart Contract Risk

Pendle's PT/YT splitting mechanism relies on smart contracts. While audited, there's always residual smart contract risk. Use multiple approvals carefully and verify contract addresses.

⚠️ Liquidity Risk

PT and YT markets may have limited liquidity, especially for newer maturities or assets. Large trades can move prices significantly. Stick to liquid markets or use limit orders.

⚡ Yield Volatility

YT price is highly sensitive to yield changes. If the underlying asset's yield drops sharply, YT loses value rapidly. This is a feature, not a bug — but it's risky.

⚡ Impermanent Loss in LP

Providing liquidity in PT/YT pools exposes you to impermanent loss similar to AMM LP positions. The PT/YT relationship can diverge from initial pricing assumptions.

🔄 Roll-over Risk

For long-term strategies, repeated roll-overs at each maturity introduce execution risk and potential slippage. Each maturity cycle is a new trade that may have different conditions.
